briefing.summary: Dive 3,800 m to the wreck of RMS Titanic, lost on 15 April 1912. Find and scan the bow and stern sections, which lie about 600 m apart on the seabed, then survey the boiler field and debris near the stern.
facts: The wreck was found on 1 September 1985 by a French–American team led by Jean-Louis Michel and Robert Ballard.
The ship broke apart as it sank. The bow faces roughly north, and the stern turned around as it fell, so its rear end points back at the bow.
By default you start beside the first objective. With a surface start you begin at the surface about 2 km north-north-west of the bow. Head south-south-east (about 150°) and descend.
The open bathymetry is too coarse to show the wreck itself.
hazards: Sunlight fades with depth; use your lights to read the deeper terrain.
Crushing pressure: about 380 atmospheres at the seabed. Your Class B hull is rated to 6,500 m.
Fragile, collapsing structure: decks and railings are still falling. Keep a respectful distance and do not touch.
Deep currents sweep the site and stir up sediment that reduces visibility.
briefing.memorial_note: Titanic is the final resting place of about 1,500 people who died on 15 April 1912. Observe, photograph and leave the wreck undisturbed.

objectives.title: Scan the bow
objectives.hint: Find the upright bow at the north end of the wreck area, around 3,790 m.

objectives.title: Scan the stern
objectives.hint: Head roughly 700 m south from the bow to the damaged stern, around 3,795 m.

objectives.title: Survey the boiler field
objectives.hint: Look east of the stern for the boilers in the debris, around 3,795 m.

objectives.title: Visit the memorial plaque site
objectives.hint: Find the former plaque site on the stern, south of the bow, near 3,790 m.
